children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Great! To get started, I need to understand a bit about your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child or children you're claiming for:**

Could you tell me:
1. How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?
2. What are their names?
3. How old are they (or what are their dates of birth)?

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies to each child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is 18 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), his eligibility will depend on whether he's in approved education or training. Let me check this with you:

**Is Alex currently enrolled in approved education or training?**

This would include:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below)
- Approved training programs (like certain apprenticeships or vocational training)

The education/training must be for more than 12 hours per week on average of supervised study or course-related work experience.

Is Alex in this type of education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and went straight into work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 18 and not in approved education or training, let me navigate through the decision tree to determine his eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to ask one more important question:

**Did Alex leave education or training recently?**

Specifically, has he left approved education or training within the last 20 weeks? If so, there may be an extension period during which you could still claim Child Benefit.

When did Alex finish school?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a while back now - it's been well over 20 weeks. He went straight into his job after finishing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: Not Eligible

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why Alex doesn't qualify:

For young people aged 16-19, Child Benefit is only available if they are in **approved education or training**. This includes:
- Full-time non-advanced education (A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below)
- Approved training programs

Since Alex:
- Is 18 years old
- Is not currently in approved education or training
- Left school more than 20 weeks ago (beyond the extension period)

He doesn't meet the qualifying criteria.

### What you should know:

There is normally a **20-week extension period** after a young person leaves education, but this has already passed in Alex's case.

### If circumstances change:

If Alex decides to return to approved education or training in the future, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him again (as long as he's still under 20 years old).

If you have any questions or if Alex's situation changes, feel free to reach out to HMRC's Child Benefit Office for further guidance.

Additionally, if a young person has recently left education, there is a 20-week extension period available, but Alex left school well beyond this timeframe. Therefore, Alex does not meet the qualifying child criteria for Child Benefit.
